spike-island-cork: A fortress island in Cork harbour, once the world's largest prison, today an award-winning museum reached by ferry.
garnish-island: A garden island in Glengarriff harbour, famous for its Italian gardens, Martello tower and the seals seen on the boat trip.
blackrock-castle-observatory: A 16th-century castle turned astronomical science observatory on the banks of the River Lee.
cork-city-gaol: A former Victorian prison with wax figures and an audio guide covering two centuries of prison life.
english-market-cork: A historic 18th-century covered market, a temple of Cork gastronomy with stalls of fish, cheeses and baked goods.
vandeleur-walled-garden: A restored 19th-century walled garden, with a Victorian glasshouse and a café, in west Clare.
craggaunowen: A living-history park recreating prehistoric and medieval Ireland, with a crannóg and a fortified house.
spanish-point-beach: A sandy bay with calm waters and history linked to the Spanish Armada, popular with families and surfers.
holy-island-inis-cealtra: A holy island on Lough Derg with a 7th-century monastery, stone cells and ancient crosses.
scattery-island: A monastic island in the Shannon estuary, with a round tower, church ruins and a seal colony.
ennis-friary: A 13th-century Franciscan friary with notable medieval carvings, in the centre of Ennis.
thoor-ballylee: A 14th-century Norman tower where the poet W.B. Yeats lived, called by him "the most beautiful place on earth".
portumna-castle-gardens: A 17th-century fortified mansion on the shores of Lough Derg, with restored gardens and a forest park.
coole-park: A nature reserve and former Lady Gregory estate, heart of the Irish Literary Revival.
brigits-garden: Gardens inspired by the Celtic festivals, with a sun garden, ancient woodland and a natural playground.
galway-city-museum: A modern museum on the history of Galway, from the medieval period to the culture of the Aran Islands.
spanish-arch-long-walk: A 16th-century arch on the River Corrib and the colourful houses of the Long Walk, a Galway postcard view.
dowth: The third great passage tomb of Brú na Bóinne, 5,000 years old, open to guided visits.
sonairte-ecology-centre: An ecology centre and organic garden on a historic farm near the sea, with trails and a vegetarian café.
kells-historic-town: A historic monastic town, former home of the Book of Kells, with high crosses and a round tower.
bective-abbey: Ruins of a 12th-century Cistercian abbey on the banks of the River Boyne, a filming location for Braveheart.
emerald-park: A theme park and zoo (formerly Tayto Park) with roller coasters, a zoo and attractions for the whole family.
wicklow-way: Ireland's oldest long-distance trail: 131 km through the Wicklow Mountains, from Dublin to Clonegal.
mount-usher-gardens: Romantic gardens on the banks of the River Vartry, with plants from all over the world and a wild-garden style.
killruddery-house-gardens: A 17th-century mansion still lived in, with formal gardens, an orangery and a farmers' market on Saturdays.
